QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_38

question.text: Under SAS-500, CO2e avoided must be reported using an accepted methodology. The MOST accepted international protocol is:

answer.text: GHG Protocol (WBCSD/WRI) Corporate Standard, with Scope 1/2/3 boundary definition and explicit emission factors cited

explanation.text: The Logic: The Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol, jointly developed by WBCSD and WRI, is the globally accepted standard for corporate greenhouse-gas accounting. It defines Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (energy indirect), and Scope 3 (other indirect) emissions and requires explicit emission-factor disclosure. CO2e-avoided claims should be reported under such an accepted methodology with clearly defined boundaries. The Trap: Options B, C and D — an in-house calculator, personal estimation, or a random number — are not standardised methodologies and cannot be independently verified. Note: The cited SIA workbook pages mention environmental/climate themes under SAS-500 and general standards knowledge, but do not specifically cite the GHG Protocol, WBCSD/WRI, Scope 1/2/3 boundaries, or emission-factor methodology. The framing above reflects general environmental-reporting practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
